source_review.notes: Checked current official TPC benchmark/version guidance; Apache Beam Nexmark, Hadoop GridMix, Spark, and Flink documentation; Kubernetes and Prometheus monitoring guidance; the NIST/SEMATECH statistical handbook; and current SPEC Cloud materials. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Standard-suite, runtime, telemetry, and compliance claims are attributed and bounded.

evidence: Reviewed offered, accepted, attempted, correct completed work, duration, throughput, goodput ratio, latency, backlog, utilization, service demand, cost efficiency, and paired-trial notation.
Checked dimensional consistency for completed work per time, busy time per completion, utilization, backlog conservation, records per second, and elapsed-time speedup.
Checked that log paired improvement has a positive direction when candidate elapsed time is smaller and that ratios retain their named numerator and denominator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every rate and ratio requires aligned work, population, resource, and time boundaries; the chapter does not treat submission or acceptance as completion.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced five trials, 12,000,000,000 records, baseline mean 1,202.0 seconds, and candidate mean 986.0 seconds.
Recomputed baseline and candidate useful throughput as 9.983 and 12.170 million records per second respectively.
Recomputed ratio-of-means speedup as 1.2191 and paired speedups as 1.2323, 1.2165, 1.1990, 1.2132, and 1.2347.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture demonstrates transparent arithmetic, not statistical sufficiency; a real decision also requires raw distributions, independent blocks, intervals, correctness, cost, and operational guardrails.

evidence: Verified useful throughput is correct completed work divided by the declared interval and the completion-goodput ratio is completed divided by offered work.
Derived the utilization identity from busy time divided by duration and service demand as busy time divided by completions, yielding utilization equals throughput times demand.
Verified backlog change is the time integral of accepted input rate minus correct output/removal rate under the stated conservation boundary.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The utilization law is an accounting relation, not a causal or capacity guarantee when workload mix, resource capacity, or measurement boundaries change.

evidence: Reviewed empty, tiny, cold, warm, skewed, compressed, partitioned, late, duplicate, null, failure, recovery, maintenance, and overload workloads.
Reviewed load-generator saturation, telemetry overhead, sink throttling, clock error, coordinated omission, cache contamination, autoscaling lag, quotas, and noisy neighbors.
Reviewed failed/censored trials, wrong output, asynchronous commits, growing backlog, timeouts, trial dependence, order drift, outliers, and noncomparable configurations.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Batch, streaming, cold-start, steady-state, burst, recovery, and shared-cluster claims are kept as distinct benchmark populations.

evidence: Traced semantic equivalence through schemas, nulls, duplicates, ordering, windows, numeric tolerance, output multiplicity, durable commits, and independent result oracles.
Checked conservation across offered, accepted, queued, completed, retried, failed, expired, duplicate, and speculative work.
Checked reproducibility from immutable code/configuration/data/environment identities through run manifests, raw evidence, validation outputs, and deterministic calculations.
invariant_checking.notes: A performance result becomes eligible only after its correctness gate passes; exclusions and boundary changes remain explicit.

evidence: Reviewed conservation proof for backlog growth and the resulting rejection of accepted-input rate as sustainable throughput when output lags.
Reviewed the service-demand/utilization identity and its limits under changing resource or workload boundaries.
Reviewed paired blocking and randomized-order argument as variance/bias controls without overstating generalization beyond sampled conditions.
proof_review.notes: Repetition and confidence intervals quantify selected uncertainty but cannot cure workload irrelevance, biased exclusions, semantic inequivalence, or hidden bottlenecks.

evidence: Audited benchmark contract, SUT, workload model, open/closed loop, warm-up, steady state, goodput, service demand, coordinated omission, paired comparison, and disclosure terminology.
Confirmed TPC-derived internal work is not labeled standards-compliant and compliance is tied to full rules, audits, disclosure, and fair-use obligations.
Confirmed ratio-of-means, paired ratios, latency percentiles, burst peaks, sustainable capacity, and cost efficiency are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Mathematical identities and experimental design mechanisms are presented with their assumptions and validity limits.

evidence: Reviewed raw workload counts, latency histograms, backlog/watermark lag, stage/task/partition distributions, CPU, memory, GC, state, storage, network, shuffle, spill, queues, throttles, and costs.
Reviewed segmentation by run, suite, workload, query, data, stage/task/partition, node/resource, topology, cache state, allocation, time block, failure, version, and configuration.
Confirmed attempts, accepted work, correct completions, failures, timeouts, retries, speculative losers, and excluded observations remain separately observable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Best-run selection, averaged percentiles, one long correlated stream, or unmeasured driver headroom is not mislabeled as reproducible comparative evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed benchmark decisions, boundaries, workload portfolios, semantic equivalence, data/environment control, warm-up, open/closed load, completion, sustainable throughput, distributions, demands, fair comparisons, uncertainty, failure, cost, and reproducibility.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable run manifests, immutable inputs, randomized paired blocks, generator-headroom tests, correctness gates, saturation sweeps, failure injection, full cost boundaries, raw evidence retention, and compliance-safe labeling. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from benchmark vocabulary and accounting identities through workload/environment control, sustainable load, statistical comparison, recovery, and disclosure. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover arithmetic, backlog, omission, pairing, completion, demand, cost, correctness, and publication.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external TPC/SPEC/NIST/Beam/Hadoop/Spark/Flink/Kubernetes/Prometheus maintainer, benchmark auditor, experimental-design/statistics/performance/runtime/storage/network/platform/SRE/security/economics specialist, production operator, downstream decision maker, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
